name: Pre-contest tanning and shaving

card.summary: Bodybuilders tan and remove body hair before a show so the stage lights show off muscle definition and shape.
card.note: Tanning exposure carries ordinary skin-damage risks.

quick.overview:
Most bodybuilders tan and shave their bodies before competing [1]. The aim is a cleaner, more defined look on stage, where smooth, darker skin shows muscle separation.

Shaving removes hair that can hide the muscle outline, and tanning darkens the skin for contrast under lights. Both sit alongside diet, water and carbohydrate manipulation in the final days before a show.
quick.how: Competitors in forum logs describe a full-body shave with an exfoliation in the days before a show, and start tanning earlier in prep; one forum user asked whether to tan as early as possible [2][3].
quick.risks: UV tanning carries skin-damage risks, and shaving can cause irritation. Final-stage dehydration, separate from this, is cited as a risk in bodybuilding generally [1].

lead: Pre-contest tanning and shaving are standard grooming steps for bodybuilders. Wikipedia notes that most bodybuilders tan and shave before competition [1].

They sit in the final stage of prep with carbohydrate loading and dehydration aimed at maximizing definition [1]. Competitors on T Nation describe a full-body shave and skin exfoliation a few days out from a show [3].

chain: Muscle shape and separation read clearly on stage
angle.text: Hairless, tanned skin makes the muscle outline easier to see on stage.

infobox: Days to weeks before a show [3]

paras: Competitors describe a full-body shave and skin exfoliation shortly before a show [3], and forum members ask about starting tanning early in prep [2].
Judges rank conditioning, muscularity, posing, symmetry and presentation [1].
